# XState declaration compatibility artifact

This internal companion is not an official XState release or an independently maintained Workflow implementation. Its identity is `xstate@5.33.2-dh.1`, derived from the public MIT-licensed `xstate@5.33.2` npm archive. Original license, runtime, entry points and native actor contracts are preserved. See the included `xstate-provenance.json` for upstream and companion SHA256, changed-member hashes and all 132 expected file hashes. Upstream: https://registry.npmjs.org/xstate/-/xstate-5.33.2.tgz

Only `dist/declarations/src/types.d.ts` and the package version metadata differ. Under `export type StateSchema = {`, change `id?: string;` to `id?: string | undefined;` and `states?: Record<string, StateSchema>;` to `states?: Record<string, StateSchema> | undefined;`. No runtime code changed. To reproduce, verify the original archive hash, extract into a scratch directory, apply exactly these two changes, set package.json version to 5.33.2-dh.1 (JSON.stringify with two spaces and final LF), and use npm 11.19.0 pack --ignore-scripts; verify the member set and hashes before accepting any newly produced archive. The committed archive is the pinned input; a repack with different archive bytes is not silently accepted.

Repository npm ci installs the pinned local archive without scripts; build verifies all members and explicitly prepares the SDK's bundled dependency even when npm workspace hoists it. The normal SDK package includes the verified bundle and this companion archive. No install hook, network registry for the modified version, or consumer-side node_modules editing is required. SDK-only apps have no need to import XState. An app that directly imports native actor constructors from xstate must declare its own direct dependency on this exact companion (copy the archive to an app-owned vendor directory and use a relative file dependency); do not rely on a transitive hoist. The app and SDK copies have the same version and bytes; the installed actor consumer gate verifies real cross-package native input/output typing and execution. Do not mix an unrelated upstream version and claim the same strict qualification. Both deployment paths are qualified for npm, not an assertion about every package manager.

When a compatible official upstream version exists, verify the original strict profile, native actor type negatives and regression gates, replace this temporary companion and remove the packaging special case. No separate runtime, fork repository or public npm publication has been created.
